title: Lockout/Tagout Program Check (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147)
subtitle: Check a US general-industry energy control program and one live lockout against OSHA's lockout/tagout standard.
regulation_line: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
instructions: Work through each item at the machine or with the program documents in hand. Record what you see, not what the procedure says should happen.
This checklist covers federal OSHA general industry only. Construction, maritime, electrical work and state-plan states may have extra or different rules.

sections.title: Program and written procedures
items: The energy control program has procedures, employee training and periodic inspections
All three parts exist and are current for the machines in use
A documented procedure exists for each machine, or all eight exception conditions are met
Written procedure on file, or all eight conditions in the note exist for that machine
Procedures state scope, purpose, authorization, rules, techniques and the means to enforce compliance
Each element appears in the written procedure
Procedures include specific requirements for testing to verify that energy controls are effective
A named verification method for each machine
Any common procedure identifies the equipment it covers
Equipment listed at least by type and location

sections.title: Locks, tags and isolating devices
items: Lockout is used wherever the energy isolating device can be locked out
Lockable devices carry locks. Where tags are used instead, the employer's demonstration of full employee protection is on file
Tags used on lockable devices go where the lock would have gone and are backed by extra measures
Tag at the lock location, plus a measure such as a removed valve handle, an opened extra disconnect or a blocked controlling switch
Lockout devices use a positive means to hold the isolating device in a safe position
Key or combination locks, blank flanges or bolted slip blinds
Tags are legible and understandable to everyone in the area
Readable wording that all authorized, affected and other employees in the area can understand
No push button or selector switch is being relied on as the isolation point
Isolation at breakers, disconnects, line valves or blocks, not at control circuit devices

sections.title: Applying controls (observe a live lockout)
items: Affected employees are notified before controls are applied
Notice given by the employer or the authorized employee before shutdown
Only the authorized employees doing the work apply locks or tags
Each worker applies their own device. Nobody affixes another person's
Every energy isolating device needed is located and operated
All sources isolated, not only the main disconnect
Stored or residual energy is dissipated or restrained
Springs, capacitors, raised parts, flywheels and pressurized lines grounded, blocked, repositioned or bled down
Isolation is verified before work starts and controls are returned to off
No personnel exposed, a start attempt or test made, controls back in the neutral or off position

sections.title: Release and special situations
items: Each lock or tag is removed by the employee who applied it
If someone else removed it, a documented and trained removal procedure was followed under the employer's direction
Affected employees are told after devices are removed and before restart
Notification recorded or observed before startup
Temporary re-energization for testing or positioning is limited to that task
Equipment deenergized and locked or tagged out again straight afterwards
Group lockouts give every authorized employee a personal device on the group lockbox
Personal locks or tags applied at the start of each person's work and removed when that person stops
Shift changes and outside contractors are covered
Written transfer method between shifts, and an exchange of procedures with each contractor

sections.title: Inspection and training
items: Each energy control procedure was inspected within the last year
Done by an authorized employee other than those using the procedure, with a demonstration
The inspection certification is complete
Machine or equipment, date, employees included and the person who inspected
Authorized employees are trained in energy recognition and isolation methods
Training covers energy sources, type and magnitude, and the means of isolation and control
Retraining follows changes in job, equipment, process or procedure
Retraining records dated after each change

references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 Appendix A, Typical minimal lockout procedures (non-mandatory)
OSHA Directive STD 01-05-019, Inspection Procedures and Interpretive Guidance
